question: How many vision tokens are needed to decode a given number of text tokens, i.e. can a page image serve as a compressed representation of text for LLM long context?
hypothesis: Rendering text as images and encoding with a compact high-resolution vision encoder can compress text tokens by roughly 10x with little loss, and larger ratios degrade like forgetting.
contributions: Quantitative analysis of vision-text token compression ratios on Fox
DeepEncoder: window attention (SAM) serially connected to global attention (CLIP) through a 16x convolutional compressor, low activation memory at high resolution
DeepSeek-OCR (DeepEncoder + DeepSeek-3B-MoE) reaching state-of-the-art among end-to-end models on OmniDocBench with the fewest vision tokens, plus chart/chemical/geometry/natural image parsing

method.summary: A VLM with a ~380M DeepEncoder (SAM-base 80M, 2-layer conv 16x token compressor, CLIP-large 300M) feeding a DeepSeek-3B-MoE decoder (570M active). Trained in two stages (encoder alone with next-token prediction, then the full model) on OCR 1.0, OCR 2.0, general vision and text-only data; evaluated for vision-text compression on Fox and for document parsing on OmniDocBench.

models.name: DeepSeek-OCR
models.architecture: DeepEncoder (SAM-base patch 16 window attn + 2-layer conv 16x compressor + CLIP-large global attn, patch embed removed) + DeepSeek-3B-MoE decoder
models.init_from: SAM-base and CLIP-large pretrained weights (inferred: 'benefit from the pretraining gains')

other.conv_compressor: 2 layers, kernel 3, stride 2, padding 1, channels 256 to 1024
other.modes: Tiny 512 (64 tok), Small 640 (100), Base 1024 (256), Large 1280 (400), Gundam n x 640 tiles + 1024 global (n*100+256), Gundam-M 1024 tiles + 1280 global (n*256+400); n in 2..9; Gundam-M by continued training on 6M sampled data

training.optimizer: AdamW (encoder stage: cosine annealing; full model: step-based scheduler)
training.epochs: 2 (encoder stage); not stated for full model
training.hardware: 20 nodes x 8 A100-40G (full model); pipeline parallel 4 parts, DP 40

other.freezing: SAM and compressor frozen in PP0, CLIP unfrozen in PP1, 6 decoder layers each on PP2 and PP3
other.no_sft: no SFT stage; model is not a chatbot
other.encoder_stage_data: all OCR 1.0 and 2.0 data + 100M LAION samples, with a compact language model (Iyer et al., OPT-IML)

limits: OCR is only a proxy; authors say OCR alone is insufficient to validate true context optical compression and plan digital-optical interleaved pretraining and needle-in-a-haystack tests.
Compression test uses only 100 English Fox pages; some bins have 4-7 pages; single run, no variance.
Fox output format mismatch means reported precision is a lower bound by the authors' account; precision metric not formally defined.
Above 10x, accuracy declines (layout complexity, blur at 512/640 resolution).
Forgetting mechanism and multi-turn dialogue compression (Fig 13, Sec 5) are conjecture, not tested.
No SFT stage; not a chatbot; no ablations of DeepEncoder design; training data not released; no warmup, precision, step counts or weight decay reported.
Reasoning ability of an LLM over compressed vision tokens is not measured; only transcription.
